A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Thompson-CHM research. Their main text, equations, figures, algorithms, and complete Appendix A support reliable comparison after matching renumbered sections and relocated material.

before.justification: v3 Section 6 and Figures 1–2 report original simulations of Thompson-CHM, measuring sample complexity and sampling proportions for seven Bernoulli arms.

after.justification: v4 Section 7 and Figures 1–2 retain these original simulation results. Results retained from v3 still qualify as original empirical outcomes.

M1.justification: The stopping rules, conditional posterior sampling, allocation parameters, interval extension, and higher-dimensional Algorithm 2 remain unchanged. The added proof explanation does not alter the procedure.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same one-dimensional synthetic problem with seven Bernoulli arms having means 0.1 through 0.7, under the same feasible and infeasible scenarios. No additional application or dataset is evaluated.

E2.justification: Both compare Thompson-CHM with theoretical sample-complexity and optimal-allocation targets, without empirical competing algorithms. The additional related-work citations introduce no evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The Beta prior, stopping-threshold function, threshold grids, normalized sample-complexity metric, and sampling-proportion measurements are retained. Figure 2 still examines thresholds 0.25 and 0.9.

E4.justification: The threshold sweep and empirical sampling-allocation analysis in Figures 1–2 are unchanged. Neither the main text nor the appendices add ablations, robustness tests, or case studies.

E5.justification: Figure 2 reports 100 repetitions in both versions. Neither version adds seed information, confidence intervals, error bars, significance tests, or another uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: The four plot panels underlying Figures 1–2 are identical, and the accompanying numerical-results passages retain the same findings. No result values, curves, rankings, or result entries change.

T1.justification: Theorems 1–5, assumptions, lemmas, and Appendix A proofs are retained. The new Section 5.2 proof sketch summarizes the posterior-concentration argument already present in v3 Appendix A.1.3. Decision-rule notation and equation-formatting edits do not change the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, three introductory contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about one-dimensional sample complexity and asymptotic optimality, the interval extension, and the potential higher-dimensional extension.

C2.justification: The interpretations of sampling allocation and agreement with theory remain unchanged. Both retain the oracle-access requirement and unresolved aspects of the higher-dimensional extension; the added proof explanation reiterates existing appendix reasoning.

D1.justification: Both disclose the same Beta prior, threshold formula, and adoption of the same cited threshold implementation. No implementation instructions, hyperparameters, hardware information, or code/data-access resources are added or removed.

R1.justification: New Section 2 adds focused discussion of thresholding bandits and fair sampling/minimax Pareto fairness, supported by seven additional cited works. This expands connections already introduced in v3 without redefining the central novelty claim.

P1.justification: v4 adds a related-work section and a main-text proof overview, makes local grammar and notation edits, and removes the NSF acknowledgment. The remaining narrative and appendix organization are largely retained.

P2.justification: Figures 1–2 retain their plots, axes, legends, and captions but are grouped together on v4 page 12, interrupting the opening conclusion paragraph. Equation displays also receive limited formatting changes; no figure or table is added or removed.

improvement.justification: The new related-work section and Section 5.2 overview of the existing proof modestly improve context and readability. These gains outweigh the small losses from removing the funding acknowledgment and interrupting the conclusion with figures. The scientific results and supporting evidence remain unchanged.
